insertion_points.what: Module docstring 'Exit codes' section rewritten: rc=2 now also covers a missing/unusable frozen per-case 'expected' declaration decided BEFORE any case is judged (verdict "no_verdict"); rc=3 now also covers a raised exception whose exact type name != declared 'expected'. Adds the REM-21/M17-M20 propagation note stating isinstance() must NOT be used.

NEW frozen-declaration precondition, evaluated immediately after cases.json is loaded and BEFORE the product import and any case judging: unusable_declared = ids whose 'expected' is not a non-empty string; cases_declared_ok = not unusable_declared; no_verdict_reason = 'cases_json_declared_expectation_missing:<ids>'; declared_expectations_cases_json = sorted distinct declarations.

Per-case loop: declared = case.get('expected') replaces the hard subscripts case['expected'] (so a DELETED key is survivable and yields a no-verdict instead of a KeyError crash); entry gains the raw 'declared' key while keeping the existing 'expected' key unchanged.

Non-raising branch now also emits declared_expectation_ok=None, declared_expectation_mismatch=False, declared_expectation_not_met=None, declared_expectation_comparison, judged=True, keeping the existing verdict 'FAIL_not_rejected'.

NEW unusable-declaration branch (precedence): declared_usable=False -> judged=False and verdict 'NOT_JUDGED_declaration_unusable'; declared_expectation_mismatch is explicitly False so an unusable declaration can never be counted as a mismatch.

NEW gating comparison: declared_ok = (entry['raised'] == declared), i.e. EXACT exception type-name equality, never isinstance(). Verdict precedence FAIL_wrong_exception_type (raised type is not ModelRegistryError) -> FAIL_declared_expectation_mismatch (right type, wrong declared name) -> PASS_rejected.

result['negative_summary'] extended ADDITIVELY (total/passed/failed unchanged in name and meaning) with declared_expectations_in_cases_json, declared_expectation_comparison, declared_expectations_enforced=true, not_judged, judged.

Exit-code classification: unusable declaration takes PRECEDENCE over case judging (verdict 'no_verdict', rc=2); negatives_ok is computed over JUDGED cases only so a NOT_JUDGED case can never by itself produce rc=3; rc=0/3 unchanged otherwise (this runner still has NO rc=1). result['no_verdict_reason'] added; exit_code_semantics gains cases_json_declared_expectations_usable, declared_expectation_mismatch_case_ids, declared_expectation_not_met_case_ids, declaration_unusable_case_ids and the reason_namespace note.
